messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Incident created: GPU autoscaler hitting max node group size — queuing and tail-latency for hosted inference. Pager sent to oncall (maria). Please join thread and follow runbook 'gpu_autoscale_failure'.

maria (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing a spike in queued requests for model-bert-xxl in region-us-west1. Dashboard shows sustained queue growth and token throttling. ETA for initial triage 5m.

sophie (sre): Confirmed: cluster-autoscaler logs show 'scale up blocked: max nodes reached for ASG gpu-pool-usw1 (desired=21, max=21)'. Pods Pending count: 47. Some pods are stuck Pending due to 'insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'.

james (engineer): We're getting 429s from the hosted API. Error payloads show 'RateLimited: no available GPU capacity'. Customer-facing error rate ~6% for /v1/generate on the tiered hosted endpoints. Not yet a total outage but definitely user impact for larger contexts.

lee (infra): Copy. Looking at cloud console -> managed instance group: max size set to 21 per policy. Reason: previous cost control guardrails. I can raise to 40 but need manual approval from infra lead, and it might take ~8-12m to spin up additional GPU nodes. Opening a manual cap-raise request now.

maria (oncall): Short-term mitigation: can we drain low-priority jobs and move them to CPU-only fallbacks? Also enable autoscaler fallback to smaller model variants (bert-medium) for ephemeral workloads. James, can your service accept a model fallback flag?

james (engineer): Yes, we have a fallback toggle. I'll push a temporary rule to route new requests for non-enterprise customers to bert-medium for next 30 minutes. Pushing config change now: 
```bash
# route fallback for non-enterprise
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://controlplane/api/v1/routepatch" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","fallback_model":"bert-medium","criteria":{"customer_tier":"standard"}}'
```
Applying — will monitor.

helga (cust-success): Heads-up: two mid-market customers already reported increased latencies. I'm pinging their CSMs with a brief note and will escalate if it becomes a wider impact.

sophie (sre): For triage notes: running quick queries: 
```bash
kubectl get pods -A | grep Pending | wc -l
# -> 47
kubectl describe pod <pending-pod> | sed -n '1,120p'
# shows events: failed scheduling: 0/21 nodes are available: 21 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```
Cluster-autoscaler event log: 
"Scale down forbidden: too many pods waiting" then "Scale up blocked by max nodes".

lee (infra): Manual request submitted to infra-leads for ASG cap bump to 40 (ticket INFRA-7421). Also opened cloud quota request with provider for additional GPU quota (convincing them we need ephemeral capacity). I'm starting the scale operation as soon as lead approves — expected node ready time ~9 minutes after start.

maria (oncall): Good. Action items: 
- james: confirm fallback routing is active and measure 95th pct latency for standard customers (report in 5m)
- lee: confirm cap bump request and ETA, post cloud console link
- sophie: continue to monitor queue length and cluster-autoscaler events
- helga: keep CSMs informed
I'll stay until handoff.

james (engineer): Fallback applied. 95p for /v1/generate (standard) dropped from 2.8s -> 1.1s. Error rate for standard tier down to 1.2%. Sending metrics to thread.

sophie (sre): Queue length stabilizing but not yet shrinking: currently 620 queued tokens/sec -> 400 queued tokens/sec since fallback. cluster-autoscaler still at max nodes.

lee (infra): Infra lead approved. Initiated manual scale: ASG target 40 -> now scaling. Cloud console: https://cloud.example.com/console/compute/instances?group=gpu-pool-usw1 (will paste events).

incident-bot: Update: manual action recorded by lee at 1770012500 — ASG increase requested (21 -> 40).

maria (oncall): Noted. Once new nodes start joining, we'll see pods schedule. If any pods remain Pending for >10min we should consider pre-creating pods or increasing pod disruption budgets? Sophie, thoughts?

sophie (sre): We'll watch for binpacking issues (GPU-affinity). If scheduler struggles, we can temporarily relax anti-affinity for the pool. Also have a plan B: enable CPU fallback for long-running batch jobs to free up GPU slots.

lee (infra): First new GPU node registered at 1770012585. 6 nodes up so far. Scaling still in progress.

maria (oncall): Handing to lee and sophie for continued watch. I'll update incident channel with a summary for postmortem and notify on-call rotation for next shift. Helga — can you prepare a short customer-facing note?

helga (cust-success): Drafting a brief: "We observed elevated latencies due to GPU capacity constraints; we applied fallbacks and increased capacity; node provisioning is underway; some customers may have seen transient errors. We'll follow up with details." Will share in 10m.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to 'mitigated' at 1770012768 by lee. Notes: manual ASG cap raise + service fallback applied; monitoring.

lee (infra): Confirming final: ASG now at 40, cluster reports 38 schedulable GPU nodes, Pending pods drained to 3 (scaling remainder). Error rate down to 0.3% and queues returning to baseline. Will file postmortem with timeline, root cause was conservative max node guardrail + bursty traffic pattern and autoscaler not configured to account for recent rollout of larger models.

sophie (sre): Adding runbook update: annotate that autoscaler max should be reviewed on deploys that increase per-request GPU usage.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. I'll close the pager in 30m after monitoring. Leaving incident open for postmortem ownership.
